results.title: Power subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a group $G$ and a natural number $n$, $G^n$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by the $n$-th powers $g^n$ of all elements $g \in G$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 11.74(a) (infinite power quotients of hyperbolic groups)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every word-hyperbolic group $G$ that is not virtually cyclic (non-elementary), there is an integer $n \ge 1$ such that the subgroup $G^n$ generated by the $n$-th powers of the elements of $G$ has infinite index in $G$, i.e. the quotient $G / G^n$ is infinite.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 11.74(b) (trivial intersection of power subgroups)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every word-hyperbolic group $G$ that is not virtually cyclic (non-elementary), the only element of $G$ lying in the subgroup $G^n$ generated by the $n$-th powers for every integer $n \ge 1$ is the identity, i.e. $\bigcap_{n \ge 1} G^n = 1$.

results.title: Non-elementary hyperbolic groups have infinite power quotients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every word-hyperbolic group $G$ that is not virtually cyclic, there is an integer $n \ge 1$ such that the subgroup $G^n$ generated by the $n$-th powers of the elements of $G$ has infinite index in $G$, i.e. the quotient $G / G^n$ is infinite.

results.title: Power subgroups of a non-elementary hyperbolic group intersect trivially
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every word-hyperbolic group $G$ that is not virtually cyclic, the only element of $G$ lying in the subgroup $G^n$ generated by the $n$-th powers for every integer $n \ge 1$ is the identity, i.e. $\bigcap_{n \ge 1} G^n = 1$.

results.title: A $1$-periodic entire function bounded by $C e^{|\operatorname{Im} s|}$ is constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be entire with $f(s + 1) = f(s)$ for all $s \in \mathbb{C}$, and suppose there is a real constant $C$ such that $|f(s)| \le C e^{|\operatorname{Im} s|}$ for every $s$ with $0 \le \operatorname{Re} s \le 1$. Then $f$ is constant.

results.title: A nonzero entire power series with infinitely many zeros
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a sequence $(a_k)_{k \ge 0}$ of complex numbers, not all zero, such that the power series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} a_k z^k$ converges absolutely for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$ and its sum vanishes at infinitely many points $z \in \mathbb{C}$.

results.title: Entire solutions of the Fermat cubic are constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ and $g$ be entire functions with $f(z)^3 + g(z)^3 = 1$ for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$. Then $f$ and $g$ are constant.

results.title: Injective entire functions are affine
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is entire and injective, then there are $a, b \in \mathbb{C}$ with $a \ne 0$ such that $f(z) = az + b$ for all $z \in \mathbb{C}$.

results.title: Weierstrass theorem on prescribed simple zeros
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be a closed set all of whose points are isolated: for each $z \in S$ there is $\varepsilon > 0$ such that no point $w \ne z$ of $S$ satisfies $|w - z| < \varepsilon$. Then there is an entire function $f$ whose zeros are exactly the points of $S$, all of them simple: $f'(z) \ne 0$ for every $z \in S$.

results.title: Jacobian matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $f : \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^n$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$, the Jacobian matrix of $f$ at $x$ is the $n \times m$ real matrix whose $(i, j)$ entry is the partial derivative of the $i$-th component $f_i$ of $f$ in the $j$-th coordinate direction at $x$: the derivative at $t = 0$ of $t \mapsto f_i(x + t e_j)$, where $e_j$ is the $j$-th standard basis vector of $\mathbb{R}^m$. A partial derivative that does not…

results.title: Entries of the Jacobian matrix are partial derivatives
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^n$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$. For every row index $i$ and column index $j$, the $(i, j)$ entry of the Jacobian matrix of $f$ at $x$ is the derivative at $t = 0$ of $t \mapsto f_i(x + t e_j)$, where $f_i$ is the $i$-th component of $f$ and $e_j$ is the $j$-th standard basis vector of $\mathbb{R}^m$. This derivative is taken to be $0$ when it does not exist.

results.title: Jacobian entries at a point of differentiability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^n$ be differentiable at $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$. Then for every row index $i$ and column index $j$, the $(i, j)$ entry of the Jacobian matrix of $f$ at $x$ is the $i$-th coordinate of $Df(x)\, e_j$, where $Df(x)$ is the Fréchet derivative of $f$ at $x$ and $e_j$ is the $j$-th standard basis vector of $\mathbb{R}^m$.

results.title: The Jacobian is the matrix of the derivative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^n$ be differentiable at $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$. Then the Jacobian matrix of $f$ at $x$ is the matrix, in the standard bases of $\mathbb{R}^m$ and $\mathbb{R}^n$, of the Fréchet derivative of $f$ at $x$, viewed as a linear map $\mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^n$.

results.title: Jacobian of a linear map given by a matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a real $n \times m$ matrix. At every point $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$, the Jacobian matrix of the map $y \mapsto M y$ from $\mathbb{R}^m$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$ is $M$.

results.title: The Jacobian matrix computes the derivative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^n$ be differentiable at $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$, and let $J$ be the Jacobian matrix of $f$ at $x$. Then for every $v \in \mathbb{R}^m$, the product $J v$ equals $Df(x)\, v$, the Fréchet derivative of $f$ at $x$ applied to $v$.

results.title: Chain rule for Jacobian matrices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^n$, $g : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^p$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$, and write $J_h(y)$ for the Jacobian matrix of $h$ at $y$. If $f$ is differentiable at $x$ and $g$ is differentiable at $f(x)$, then $J_{g \circ f}(x) = J_g(f(x))\, J_f(x)$, a product of a $p \times n$ and an $n \times m$ matrix.

results.title: The claim of Scottish Book Problem 8
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: This is the statement, asked about in form (b) of Mazur's Problem 8 in the Scottish Book typescript, that every convergent sequence $(z_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of real numbers can be written as $z_n = \frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} x_k y_{n-k}$ for all $n \ge 0$, where $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ and $(y_n)_{n \ge 0}$ are convergent sequences of real numbers.

results.title: Mazur's Problem 8 has a negative answer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a convergent sequence $(z_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of real numbers that cannot be written as $z_n = \frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} x_k y_{n-k}$ for all $n \ge 0$ with convergent sequences $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ and $(y_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of real numbers. That is, the claim of Scottish Book Problem 8 is false.

results.title: Extended Stirling numbers of the second kind
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Knuth's extended Stirling number of the second kind at integers $n$ and $k$ is the natural number equal to the Stirling number of the second kind $S(n, k)$ if $n \ge 0$ and $k \ge 0$, equal to the unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $c(-k, -n)$ if $n < 0$ and $k < 0$, and equal to $0$ otherwise. Here $c(j, i)$ is the number of permutations of $j$ elements with exactly $i$ cycles.

results.title: Extended Stirling numbers at natural arguments
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Extended Stirling numbers at negative arguments

results.summary: For all positive integers $a$ and $b$, the extended Stirling number of the second kind at $(-a, -b)$ equals the unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $c(b, a)$, the number of permutations of $b$ elements with exactly $a$ cycles.

results.title: Values below their Bellman image lie below the policy value
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a Markov decision process with a finite set of states $S$, real rewards and stochastic transition probabilities, and let $0 \le \gamma < 1$. Let $\pi$ be a deterministic policy, with Bellman operator $T^\pi$ and value $V^\pi$. If $V : S \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfies $V(s) \le (T^\pi V)(s)$ for every state $s$, then $V(s) \le V^\pi(s)$ for every state $s$.

results.title: Policy improvement theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a Markov decision process with a finite set of states $S$, a finite nonempty set of actions $A$, real rewards and stochastic transition probabilities, and let $0 \le \gamma < 1$. Write $V^\pi$ for the value of a deterministic policy $\pi : S \to A$. For every deterministic policy $\pi$, the improved policy $\pi'$, which is greedy for $V^\pi$, satisfies $V^\pi(s) \le V^{\pi'}(s)$ for every state $s$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a Markov decision process with a finite set of states $S$, a finite nonempty set of actions $A$, real rewards and stochastic transition probabilities, and let $0 \le \gamma < 1$.
